// Follows one ECS task until it stops or the caller's time budget runs out. Every
// blocking step (each describe call and each pause between polls) is capped by the
// time left, so the caller gets its answer at the bound instead of whenever a
// fixed-length waiter happens to return. Following a task never stops or restarts it.
export const DEFAULT_TASK_POLL_MS = 5_000;
export const MAX_DESCRIBE_MS = 30_000;

export function waitForTaskStop({ describeTask, budgetMs, now = () => Date.now(), sleep = sleepSync, pollMs = DEFAULT_TASK_POLL_MS }) {
  const deadline = now() + budgetMs;
  let task = null;
  let lastError = null;
  for (;;) {
    const remaining = deadline - now();
    if (remaining <= 0) {
      return { stopped: false, task, lastError };
    }
    const described = describeTask(Math.min(remaining, MAX_DESCRIBE_MS));
    if (described.error) {
      lastError = described.error;
    } else {
      lastError = null;
      task = described.task ?? task;
      if (task?.lastStatus === "STOPPED") {
        return { stopped: true, task, lastError };
      }
    }
    const left = deadline - now();
    if (left <= 0) {
      return { stopped: false, task, lastError };
    }
    sleep(Math.min(pollMs, left));
  }
}

export function sleepSync(ms) {
  Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms);
}
